app.title: DNA Mutation Effect Predictor
app.summary: A person enters one protein-level variant as a gene symbol and a protein change, or picks a ready example, and runs the classifier; the interface fetches the protein sequence, embeds the wild-type and mutant windows, and returns a pathogenic or benign call with its probability, the parsed residues, and the variant marked on a predicted 3D structure. Each call joins a short list of recent predictions. For many variants they upload a two-column CSV instead, run the whole file with a progress bar, see the counts of each call, and download the predictions as a CSV. A separate page shows how well the classifier did on its held-out test set.

task.text: Predict whether each missense variant is likely pathogenic or benign from protein language model embeddings, one at a time or for a whole file, and save the calls.

data.text: A list of protein-level variants given as gene symbol plus HGVSp change; for each, the canonical protein sequence and a predicted structure are fetched, and the output is a label with a probability per variant.
data.item: a single missense variant: a gene and an amino-acid change at one position

stage.text: scoring candidate missense variants for likely effect, after they are identified and before follow-up

mechanism.text: A sidebar switches between a single-variant page, where a two-field form produces a verdict card, gauge, residue details and a rotatable 3D structure with the mutated residue marked, and a batch page, where an uploaded CSV is previewed, run row by row, totalled and exported. A performance page shows the classifier's confusion matrix, ROC curve, summary metrics and top features as a dashboard.

field.text: variant effect prediction with protein language models in human genetics

workflow.name: classify items with a trained model, singly or as a batch, and export the calls

steps.here: type a gene symbol and an HGVSp change into a two-field form, or click a quick example to fill it; for many variants, upload a CSV with gene and hgvsp columns (capped at 500 rows) and check the preview of its first rows, with a sample template to download

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: CLASSIFY MUTATION parses the change, looks up the protein sequence, embeds wild-type and mutant windows around the site, and scores them with the classifier, blending in a second DNA-model opinion when it is reachable; the label is set at a 0.5 probability

the verdict card shows the call, probability, inference time and the per-model breakdown, beside a gauge, a pathogenic/benign bar and the parsed wild-type residue, position and mutant residue; below, the predicted structure is drawn in 3D, coloured by distance from the mutated residue
each call is pushed onto a recent-predictions strip (last ten kept, five shown) with its label and probability, and the sidebar counts them

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: a batch run shows a progress bar row by row, then a results table and totals of pathogenic and benign calls with their shares
Download Results (CSV) saves each row's call, blended probability and component model scores as predictions.csv

steps.step: check how far the model can be trusted
steps.here: a performance page shows held-out accuracy, precision, recall, F1, specificity, MCC and AUC, a confusion matrix, an ROC curve and the most important selected embedding dimensions

distinctive: the input is written in a standard notation for an amino-acid change (HGVSp), parsed into wild-type residue, position and mutant residue before anything is computed
the reference sequence and predicted structure are fetched from public databases for each gene rather than loaded by the person
two models give separate opinions that are blended, and the breakdown is shown so the person sees when the second model was unavailable
the result is placed on a 3D protein structure with every residue coloured by its distance from the change
the classifier's own held-out performance is published alongside the predictions so each call can be weighed against it
